question: What is the main goal of doing an economic check on health care services?

options.A: Reducing the salaries of clinical nursing staff
options.B: Comparing costs and health outcomes of different programs
options.C: Eliminating all out-of-pocket spending for patients
options.D: Maximizing the number of hospital beds in a region

explanation: Economic appraisal looks at alternative treatments by weighing what they cost against their clinical results to help guide funding choices. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why do health managers need to use economic appraisals?

options.A: Private hospitals operate without any financial limitations
options.B: Healthcare resources are limited relative to community needs
options.C: Government budgets for health care never experience constraints
options.D: Clinical outcomes are identical across all treatment modalities

explanation: Because funds, staff, and supplies are always limited, health systems must choose which interventions give the best value for care. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h1)

question: If a patient pays transport fare to reach the clinic, what kind of cost is this?
explanation: Travel expenses are direct money costs caused by illness, but the money is not paid directly to the hospital or medical staff. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h2)

question: What are lost wages called when a patient misses work due to being hospitalized?
explanation: When people cannot work because of illness, the lost productivity is measured as an indirect cost in health economics. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h2)

question: When is it best to use a cost-minimization analysis?

options.A: When one intervention has far superior clinical effectiveness
options.B: When comparing programs with completely different goals
options.C: When health outcomes cannot be measured numerically
options.D: When competing interventions produce identical health outcomes

explanation: Cost-minimization is used when two options give the exact same health results, so the choice comes down to which one is cheaper. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h3)

question: A clinic checks two different brands of the same blood pressure drug that work equally well and are equally safe. Which analysis should they use?
explanation: Since the drugs have the same safety and effectiveness, the study only needs to find the least expensive option. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h3)

question: How are health results usually measured in a cost-effectiveness analysis?

options.A: Natural physical units like life-years gained

explanation: Cost-effectiveness uses real health measures like blood pressure lowered, lives saved, or extra years of life. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h4)

question: What does the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) actually measure?

options.A: Extra cost required to achieve an extra unit of health outcome
options.B: Total hospital expenditure divided by total annual admissions
options.C: Difference between nurse salaries and drug procurement costs
options.D: Net monetary benefit minus patient out-of-pocket expenses

explanation: The ICER compares how much extra money a new treatment costs against how much extra health benefit it gives. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h4)

question: What does QALY stand for in health economics?
explanation: QALY stands for Quality-Adjusted Life Year, which is a standard way to measure both the length and quality of life gained from a treatment. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why do health policy makers like using cost-utility analysis?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need to calculate financial costs of nursing care
options.B: It avoids assigning numerical values to patient quality of life
options.C: It measures clinical success exclusively through laboratory blood test values
options.D: It allows comparison of completely different types of health interventions using a common unit

explanation: Using QALYs lets health planners compare completely different programs, like mental health care versus surgical services, on the same scale. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h5)

question: What makes cost-benefit analysis different from other types of economic studies?

options.A: Outcomes are measured strictly as physical life years gained
options.B: Both costs and health outcomes are expressed in monetary terms
options.C: It ignores indirect productivity losses completely
options.D: It focuses solely on hospital administrative expenditures

explanation: Cost-benefit analysis turns health outcomes into money values so that the benefits and costs can be directly compared in currency. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is a major ethical worry about using cost-benefit analysis in health care?

options.A: Requiring complex computer software for simple arithmetic
options.B: Placing a financial monetary value on human life and health
options.C: Failing to account for nurse staffing shortages in wards
options.D: Measuring outcomes in natural units instead of currency

explanation: Many people and healthcare workers feel uncomfortable putting a direct price tag on human life and suffering. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a limitation of health economic appraisals?

options.A: Potential neglect of vulnerable or hard-to-reach populations
options.B: Guaranteed elimination of all hospital financial deficits
options.C: Reliance on assumptions that may not fit local settings
options.D: Difficulty in accurately quantifying all indirect costs

explanation: Economic studies help guide decisions and find efficient practices, but they do not automatically wipe out a hospital's money problems. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h7)

question: How can nurse managers use findings from economic appraisals in their daily work?

options.A: To replace clinical judgment with rigid financial spreadsheets
options.B: To eliminate the need for patient consent in clinical research
options.C: To determine individual nurse disciplinary actions and salary cuts
options.D: To provide evidence when advocating for cost-effective staffing and equipment

explanation: Managers can use economic data to support requests for better ward supplies and staffing without lowering the quality of care. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h7)
